reading: Each straight colour-2 segment gets a diamond of colour 8 around it: at distance d from the segment's line, the background cells over the segment's span shrunk by d at both ends become 8.

new_rows.name: diamond
new_rows.datalog:
dv(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), cell(R, XA, C), obj(O, R, XA), D = Y - R, D > 0, XA = X - D, XB = X + D, obj(O, R, XB).
uv(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), cell(R, XA, C), obj(O, R, XA), D = R - Y, D > 0, XA = X - D, XB = X + D, obj(O, R, XB).
rh(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), cell(YA, K, C), obj(O, YA, K), D = X - K, D > 0, YA = Y - D, YB = Y + D, obj(O, YB, K).
lh(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), cell(YA, K, C), obj(O, YA, K), D = K - X, D > 0, YA = Y - D, YB = Y + D, obj(O, YB, K).
diamond(Y, X) :- dv(Y, X).
diamond(Y, X) :- uv(Y, X).
diamond(Y, X) :- rh(Y, X).
diamond(Y, X) :- lh(Y, X).

why: a background cell becomes 8 exactly when, for some d >= 1, the two cells at offset d along the segment direction, d rows (or columns) away, belong to the same segment

reading: The nine non-background cells of the 5x5 X pattern are squeezed together into a 3x3 grid, keeping their relative row/column order.

slots.subject: the non-background cells (X pattern: corners, inner diagonal cells, centre)
slots.result: 3x3 grid: out[i][j] is the input cell of the X that sits at rank i among rows and rank j among columns, background removed

why: output cells are exactly the input's non-background cells in the same relative positions with empty rows/columns gaps closed

reading: The grid is 3x3 blocks of 2x2 separated by 0 lines on background 1. Where two blocks in the same block-row or block-column have the same non-background colour at the same position, the block between them gets that colour at that position.

slots.pair: two cells of the same colour c (not 1, not 0) on one row at columns x and x+6, or on one column at rows y and y+6
slots.target: the midpoint cell (x+3 or y+3), in the middle block
slots.colour: c, the colour of the pair (differs within one pair of grids, so not a constant)

why: every changed cell is the exact midpoint of two equal-coloured marks 6 apart on its row or column, and takes their colour

reading: The output is the input tiled N times across and N times down, where N is the input's side length.
why: every block of the output is an exact copy of the input; the block grid is N x N with N = input height = input width (no empty blocks)
invariants: every block identical to the input

reading: Several small shapes and one large shape (scaled up and cut by the grid edge) lie on a background; the output is the small shape whose 2x scaled version matches the visible part of the large shape.

slots.reference: the large object touching the grid border (a 2x upscaled shape, partly cut off)
slots.result: the bounding box of the candidate whose 2x upscaling agrees with the reference on its visible cells, cut from the input

why: the output equals the box of exactly one small object, and that object scaled by 2 is consistent with the border-cut large object
invariants: output is a box cut from the input
background colour kept in the cut

reading: The input is three 4x4 panels separated by colour-2 columns; they are overlaid into one 4x4 grid with the left panel (4) on top, then the middle (9), then the right (1).

slots.panels: the three stripes cut by the full colour-2 separator columns
slots.priority: left panel over middle panel over right panel
slots.result: each cell takes the first non-background value in priority order, else 0

why: every output cell equals the left panel's cell if non-zero, else the middle's if non-zero, else the right's

reading: The top-left quadrant pattern (2 colours) is reflected into the other three quadrants (left-right, up-down, both), and each copy is recoloured using the hint cells already present in that quadrant (a colour with no hint becomes 0).

slots.source: the fully drawn top-left quadrant of the square pattern
slots.copies: its mirror images in the top-right (horizontal flip), bottom-left (vertical flip) and bottom-right (180 rotation) quadrants
slots.key: per quadrant, a colour map from source colours to the colours of the hint cells at corresponding positions; unmapped colours go to 0

why: each quadrant is the matching reflection of the top-left quadrant under a quadrant-specific colour map consistent with its input hints

reading: Empty columns are deleted, then the objects are shifted up or down one after another, left to right, so that each object's left end connects to the previous object's right end, forming one continuous chain.

slots.subjects: the objects, ordered left to right
slots.shift: vertical offset of each object so its leftmost cell is in the same row as the previous object's rightmost cell (adjacent column)

why: output width = input width minus empty columns; each object keeps its shape and colour and touches its predecessor horizontally

reading: Every coloured cell extends a line of its own colour straight down to the bottom of the grid.
why: every cell below a coloured cell in its column takes that colour, up to the bottom border; nothing else changes

reading: From the single 8 cell, a colour-5 staircase is drawn up-right (up 2, right 2, repeated) and its point reflection down-left (down 2, left 2, repeated), clipped at the grid border.
why: the 5 cells form the same fixed staircase shape relative to the 8 marker in every pair (clipped by the border)
